claim: Density is not the problem, poor design is
lead: Housing quality is poor on all three islands, and density does not explain it. Plots that are not dense score as badly as dense ones: all 5 on Malé and 86% on Villimalé fall below the midpoint. Hulhumalé cannot test the idea: its 8 plots are one building type at FAR 22.5.

measures.name: Not dense plots that score poor
measures.note: % of plots below FAR 1.87 scoring under 16 of 32 (Toolkit 3)

measures.name: Dense plots that score poor
measures.note: % of plots at FAR 1.87 or above scoring under 16 of 32 (Toolkit 3)

notes: All 5 not dense plots score poor, and 68% of the 31 dense plots do. Even sparse plots fail. No plot passes 19 of 32.
86% of 35 not dense plots score poor, against 91% of 34 dense plots. Almost no difference, so density is not what separates them.
No plots that are not dense to compare. All 8 share one typology at FAR 22.5 and score 9 of 32: extreme density with no diversity or human scale.

caption.label: Figure
caption.text: Each measure scaled to its largest island.

conclusion: Plots that are not dense fail almost as often as dense ones (100% and 86% poor), so density is not what drives poor quality. Poor design is.
